documents.unit: Clark University policies (Artificial Intelligence Use Policy)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Use Policy (Rev FY26)
documents.stance_why: The policy "welcomes and encourages the use of AI" but sets no uniform classroom rule: it says expectations "should be standardized in a three-tier system" (no use, limited use, extensive use) and that "faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines". Tiers plus instructor discretion means delegates.
documents.summary: University-wide principles-based AI policy covering academic, research and administrative use. It encourages AI, requires disclosure and human responsibility, protects data, and asks faculty to use a three-tier no/limited/extensive scheme in syllabi.

units.why: Section 1 says the policy "promotes the responsible, ethical, transparent, and secure deployment of AI", a statement of purpose for the whole framework, so P56 (institution-wide framework); it sets no behavior rule.
units.anchor: promotes the responsible, ethical, transparent, and secure deployment of AI

units.why: States scope: the policy "applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates". Scope definition, so P61 rather than P56 because it says who and what is covered.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates

units.why: The sentence "AI use may not be appropriate in all contexts" is a principle-level caveat about the framework's scope; P56 as it frames the policy and sets no rule.
units.anchor: The University recognizes that AI use may not be appropriate in all contexts.

units.why: The definition of Generative AI, "AI systems capable of producing original content" including code, fixes what the policy covers; P61.
units.anchor: AI systems capable of producing original content

units.why: The definition of Agentic AI, systems that "plan and carry out multi-step tasks", extends the policy's scope to agents; P61.
units.anchor: AI systems that can independently or with human oversight plan and carry out

units.why: "Clark University welcomes and encourages the use of AI" sets a positive default toward AI in teaching, research and operations; P02, recommended not required so modality should.
units.anchor: Clark University welcomes and encourages the use of AI to spark creativity

units.why: "Responsibility for AI-assisted work rests solely with the individual(s) utilizing AI" makes users own what they produce with AI; P29.
units.anchor: Responsibility for AI-assisted work rests solely with the individual(s) utilizing AI.

units.why: "AI tools do not replace human judgment and expertise" says humans stay the decision-makers; P32.
units.anchor: AI tools do not replace human judgment and expertise.

units.why: "Users should openly communicate when AI is used" is a disclosure expectation (softened by 'should'); P24.
units.anchor: Users should openly communicate when AI is used, especially in scholarly and operational contexts.

units.why: "its use must be properly attributed and not misrepresent human authorship" requires attribution of AI use; P24.
units.anchor: its use must be properly attributed and not misrepresent human authorship.

units.why: "AI should be leveraged to expand opportunities and minimize bias" states an equity and bias principle; P53 as it names bias, not cost or access to tools (P51).
units.anchor: AI should be leveraged to expand opportunities and minimize bias

units.why: "Appropriate safeguards must be in place when using AI tools with sensitive information" protects confidential data; P50.
units.anchor: Appropriate safeguards must be in place when using AI tools with sensitive information.

units.why: "The University reserves the right to review, restrict, or discontinue any AI tools that present unacceptable risk" lets the university vet and withdraw tools; P50 (vetted tools).
units.anchor: The University reserves the right to review, restrict, or discontinue any AI tools

units.why: "augment—not replace—human judgment, critical thinking, creativity" says AI must not replace thinking; P32.
units.anchor: augment—not replace—human judgment, critical thinking, creativity, and expertise

units.why: "not a substitute for professional, medical, mental health, legal, or academic advising services" is a personal-use caution that fits no listed type (not teaching rules), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: not a substitute for professional, medical, mental health, legal, or academic advising services
units.uncovered_note: AI tools are not a substitute for professional, medical, mental health, legal or academic advising services.

units.why: "Users are expected to apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs" tells users to check AI output; P31.
units.anchor: Users are expected to apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to explore AI’s potential in their curricula" encourages instructors to try AI; P02 (encourage) with faculty as actor, not P63 since no support is offered.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore AI’s potential in their curricula

units.why: "Syllabi and assignment guidelines should be transparent about when and how AI can or cannot be used" asks for AI statements in syllabi; P09.
units.anchor: Syllabi and assignment guidelines should be transparent about when and how AI

units.why: The university says expectations "should be standardized in a three-tier system" named no use, limited use, extensive use; P05.
units.anchor: standardized in a three-tier system across the university

units.why: Defines the no-use tier: AI "not allowed to be used in completing that assignment or at all in the course"; P01 (ban) rather than P05 because this sentence states the prohibition itself.
units.anchor: AI tools are not allowed to be used in completing that assignment

units.why: Limited-use example: "AI may be used to brainstorm ideas for a paper"; P15 brainstorming.
units.anchor: AI may be used to brainstorm ideas for a paper

units.why: Same example: "cannot be used to write the paper"; P19 (AI may not produce the submitted work).
units.anchor: cannot be used to write the paper

units.why: Extensive use means "there are no restrictions on AI use for that assignment or course"; P02 (open default) for that tier.
units.anchor: there are no restrictions on AI use for that assignment or course

units.why: Even extensive use must follow the policy, "including but not limited to appropriate disclosure, labeling, and attribution"; P24.
units.anchor: appropriate disclosure, labeling, and attribution

units.why: "students are invited to leverage AI for creative inquiry, responsible collaboration, and academic advancement" where permitted; P02 encourage.
units.anchor: students are invited to leverage AI for creative inquiry, responsible collaboration

units.why: Permitted use is conditional: "provided its contribution is properly disclosed and does not undermine learning outcomes"; disclosure condition so P24.
units.anchor: provided its contribution is properly disclosed and does not undermine learning outcomes

units.why: "faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines" leaves the rule to instructors; P04.
units.anchor: faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines

units.why: "Research activities using AI must adhere to principles of integrity, ethical authorship, and appropriate attribution"; P62 research.
units.anchor: Research activities using AI must adhere to principles of integrity, ethical

units.why: "Some disciplines or instructors may choose to minimize or avoid AI use altogether. These choices are fully supported" lets instructors set stricter rules; P04.
units.anchor: Some disciplines or instructors may choose to minimize or avoid AI use altogether.

units.why: "All high-impact automated decisions must include human review" is an administrative AI rule, not about teaching and learning types; UNCOVERED (P46 is grades only).
units.anchor: All high-impact automated decisions must include human review
units.uncovered_note: High-impact automated administrative decisions must include human review.

units.why: "AI-driven solutions are encouraged for admissions, finance, financial aid, employment" encourages administrative AI; P02.
units.anchor: AI-driven solutions are encouraged for admissions, finance, financial aid, employment

units.why: "should not be used as the sole basis for decisions that materially affect individuals" restricts AI-only decisions; UNCOVERED, same note as the other administrative decision rule.
units.anchor: should not be used as the sole basis for decisions that materially affect individuals
units.uncovered_note: AI outputs should not be the sole basis for decisions materially affecting individuals; human review and validation required.

units.why: "Sensitive data may only be used with institutionally approved, contractually vetted, and security-reviewed AI tools"; P50 vetted tools.
units.anchor: Sensitive data may only be used with institutionally approved, contractually vetted

units.why: "AI tools may not be used to train external models using Clark data unless explicitly authorized" limits data sharing with AI providers; P65.
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used to train external models using Clark data

units.why: AI systems cannot be used in ways that violate rules on "library licensed content, copyrighted materials" and community IP; P52 licensing and copyright.
units.anchor: copyrighted materials created internal or external to Clark

units.why: "Users must promptly report suspected breaches or unauthorized disclosures to Information Technology Services" is incident reporting, no type fits; UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Users must promptly report suspected breaches or unauthorized disclosures
units.uncovered_note: Report suspected data breaches or unauthorized disclosures involving AI to ITS.

units.why: "The Provost oversees academic standards for AI use" assigns governance roles; P56.
units.anchor: The Provost oversees academic standards for AI use

units.why: ITS and committees "will monitor AI technology developments, review significant initiatives"; ongoing review so P54.
units.anchor: will monitor AI technology developments, review significant initiatives

units.why: "participating in relevant training or compliance programs" expects community training; P63 is closest though not faculty-only.
units.anchor: participating in relevant training or compliance programs

units.why: "responsible for the content they provide, whether the content was created using AI or not"; P29 ownership.
units.anchor: responsible for the content they provide, whether the content was created using AI or not

units.why: "Violations of this policy may result in corrective action according to existing University procedures" routes violations to existing processes; P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy may result in corrective action according to existing University procedures.

units.why: The policy "does not replace, other University policies governing academic integrity"; keeps integrity processes in force, P36.
units.anchor: does not replace, other University policies governing academic integrity

units.why: "reserves the right to intervene or restrict access to AI tools used in violation" is an enforcement power; P36 is closest.
units.anchor: Clark University reserves the right to intervene or restrict access to AI tools

units.why: "their use must be disclosed in a clear and appropriate manner" requires disclosure; P24.
units.anchor: their use must be disclosed in a clear and appropriate manner

units.why: Citation must include "a brief description of how the tool was used" plus the tool's identity; P25 (details) rather than P24.
units.anchor: a brief description of how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, editing, data analysis)

units.why: "AI use must be documented when it materially influences decisions" is administrative disclosure; P24 with admin staff.
units.anchor: AI use must be documented when it materially influences decisions

units.why: "individuals remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and ethical use of" AI-assisted content; P29.
units.anchor: individuals remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and ethical use of

units.why: "Next Review Date November, 2026" sets a review cycle; P54.
units.anchor: Next Review Date November, 2026

documents.title: Teach with AI
documents.stance_why: The page recommends "a three-tiered framework" (No use, Limited use, Extensive use) with sample syllabus language and says integrating AI "or choosing not to" is the instructor's choice. It offers tiers and templates and no single rule, so delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty guidance page from Clark's AI Hub. It gives the three-tier framework with sample syllabus language, AI assignment ideas, advice on talking with objecting students, cautions on AI detectors, and ways instructors can use AI in teaching.

units.why: Recommends "a three-tiered framework for your assignments or your course as a whole"; P05 tiers.
units.anchor: a three-tiered framework for your assignments or your course as a whole

units.why: "Integrating AI into your courses, or choosing not to, starts with clear communication" asks faculty to state expectations; P09.
units.anchor: Integrating AI into your courses, or choosing not to, starts with clear communication

units.why: No use tier: "Students do the work completely on their own without any AI help"; P01.
units.anchor: Students do the work completely on their own without any AI help

units.why: Explains no use is for steps "where the struggle is the learning"; P41.
units.anchor: where the struggle is the learning

units.why: Limited use lets students "quiz themselves" with AI; P14 study aids.
units.anchor: use it to build an outline, fix grammar, or quiz themselves

units.why: "the final writing and core ideas must still be their own" in limited use; P29.
units.anchor: the final writing and core ideas must still be their own

units.why: Limited use requires students to "disclose where and how they used AI"; P24.
units.anchor: they must disclose where and how they used AI.

units.why: Extensive use: "few or no restrictions on how the tool is used"; P02.
units.anchor: Students work directly alongside the AI with few or no restrictions

units.why: Extensive use "does not negate a student properly disclosing and attributing"; P24.
units.anchor: This level does not negate a student properly disclosing and attributing the use of AI.

units.why: Sample no-use syllabus text: "all work must be completed completely on your own without any assistance from generative AI tools"; P01.
units.anchor: all work must be completed completely on your own without any assistance from generative AI

units.why: "The only way to build those skills is to go through the cognitive struggle yourself" justifies the ban; P41.
units.anchor: The only way to build those skills is to go through the cognitive struggle yourself.

units.why: Allowed in no-use: "Standard spell-check, word processors, library databases, and course readings"; P18 writing tools.
units.anchor: Standard spell-check, word processors, library databases, and course readings.

units.why: "Using AI at any stage of your work" is not allowed, even brainstorming or outlining; P19 is closest as it bars AI contribution to submitted work.
units.anchor: Using AI at any stage of your work

units.why: "All submitted work must be entirely your own"; P29.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be entirely your own.

units.why: Sample limited-use text: "you are welcome to use generative AI tools behind the scenes as a helpful assistant"; P05 tier definition.
units.anchor: you are welcome to use generative AI tools behind the scenes as a helpful assistant

units.why: "still the one doing the heavy intellectual lifting and final writing" keeps the student as primary thinker; P32.
units.anchor: ensuring that you are still the one doing the heavy intellectual lifting and final writing

units.why: Allowed: "brainstorm topics, structure rough outlines, check your written grammar"; P15.
units.anchor: Using AI to help you brainstorm topics, structure rough outlines, check your written grammar

units.why: Allowed: AI as "a conversational study partner to quiz you on concepts"; P12 tutor.
units.anchor: act as a conversational study partner to quiz you on concepts

units.why: "You must disclose where and how you used AI in all cases"; P24.
units.anchor: You must disclose where and how you used AI in all cases.

units.why: Not allowed: "Having an AI write sentences, paragraphs, or blocks of code for your final submissions"; P19.
units.anchor: Having an AI write sentences, paragraphs, or blocks of code for your final submissions.

units.why: Sample extensive text: "You are encouraged to work directly alongside these tools"; P02.
units.anchor: You are encouraged to work directly alongside these tools

units.why: "Learning how to effectively co-create with AI is an essential professional skill"; P44.
units.anchor: Learning how to effectively co-create with AI is an essential professional skill.

units.why: "our grading will focus heavily on your human judgment" changes grading around AI; P35.
units.anchor: our grading will focus heavily on your human judgment

units.why: Allowed: "generate drafts, write code, analyze data sets, or build project components"; P16 AI code with disclosure condition.
units.anchor: Using AI to help generate drafts, write code, analyze data sets, or build project components.

units.why: "You must clearly disclose and attribute how you used the tools for every assignment"; P24.
units.anchor: You must clearly disclose and attribute how you used the tools for every assignment.

units.why: "depends entirely on the human validation step" asks students to verify and improve AI output; P31.
units.anchor: Your success in this class depends entirely on the human validation step

units.why: AI Peer Review has students "turn in both their prompt history, and a short reflection"; P26 chosen over P35 because it states what students submit.
units.anchor: They turn in both their prompt history, and a short reflection

units.why: Fact-checking idea: give students "an AI-generated paper containing fake citations or subtle errors"; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Give students an AI-generated paper containing fake citations or subtle errors.

units.why: Socratic Dialog: students "submit the chat transcript along with a paragraph summarizing what they learned"; P26.
units.anchor: submit the chat transcript along with a paragraph summarizing what they learned.

units.why: Role Plays: "Have AI play the role of a client, historical figure, or examiner"; P35 assignment design.
units.anchor: Have AI play the role of a client, historical figure, or examiner.

units.why: "Academic integrity remains the foundation of teaching and learning at Clark, regardless of whether AI tools are used" frames the rules; P56.
units.anchor: Academic integrity remains the foundation of teaching and learning at Clark

units.why: "Students are responsible for the work they submit, including any content created or informed by AI"; P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for the work they submit, including any content created or informed

units.why: "AI use should never misrepresent authorship, learning, or intellectual contribution"; P29 (own work).
units.anchor: AI use should never misrepresent authorship, learning, or intellectual contribution

units.why: "Faculty should help students understand that the responsible use of AI does not replace original thinking"; P32 directed at faculty.
units.anchor: the responsible use of AI does not replace original thinking, disciplinary knowledge, or personal accountability

units.why: AI-detection results "should not be considered definitive evidence of academic misconduct"; P39.
units.anchor: should not be considered definitive evidence of academic misconduct

units.why: Misuse concerns "should be evaluated using academic judgment, course context" and supporting evidence; no type for judging suspected misuse, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: concerns about potential misuse of AI should be evaluated using academic judgment, course context
units.uncovered_note: Evaluate suspected AI misuse using academic judgment, course context, assignment nature and supporting evidence.

units.why: "Suspected violations should be addressed through Clark’s existing academic integrity process"; P36.
units.anchor: Suspected violations should be addressed through Clark’s existing academic integrity process

units.why: "Clearly explain exactly why you are asking them to use it for this specific task" tells instructors to explain assignment expectations; P09 closest.
units.anchor: Clearly explain exactly why you are asking them to use it for this specific task.

units.why: "Offer an Equal Opt-Out Path" lets objecting students meet goals "using traditional research methods or peer collaboration"; P51.
units.anchor: meet the exact same learning goals using traditional research methods or peer collaboration instead.

units.why: Teaching use: "ask an AI to brainstorm five different real-world analogies"; P59.
units.anchor: ask an AI to brainstorm five different real-world analogies

units.why: Teaching use: "ask it to draft a detailed scoring rubric"; P59.
units.anchor: ask it to draft a detailed scoring rubric based on your specific criteria

units.why: Teaching use: instruct AI "to generate multiple-choice questions or short-answer prompts"; P59.
units.anchor: instruct it to generate multiple-choice questions or short-answer prompts

units.why: Teaching use: ask AI "to identify the top three logical traps or points of confusion"; P59.
units.anchor: ask it to identify the top three logical traps or points of confusion

units.why: Teaching use: AI can "generate a companion guide" for texts; P59.
units.anchor: ask it to generate a companion guide

units.why: "Meet with Mark Jacobs, AI Pedagogy and Curriculum Innovation Specialist" is faculty support; P63.
units.anchor: Mark partners with faculty to navigate academic integrity, design assignments, and integrate AI into courses.

units.why: Library guidance with "clear citation guidelines" and librarian appointments supports faculty learning; P63.
units.anchor: find clear citation guidelines, access specialized research support

units.why: Faculty integrating AI into research are told to visit OSPR "to navigate guidelines"; P62.
units.anchor: visit the Office of Sponsored Programs and Research (OSPR) website to navigate guidelines

units.why: "This website was drafted with generative AI assistance (Gemini and Copilot)" discloses the university's own AI use; P47.
units.anchor: This website was drafted with generative AI assistance (Gemini and Copilot)

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. UNCOVERED units: personal-advice caution, administrative AI decision human review (two), incident reporting, evaluating suspected misuse by judgment and context.
